# Sirach Chapter 3 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 3 (31 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 19

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.2: "honored the father" vs. "gave authority to the father"

**EMET:** "the Lord honored the father above the children"
**LOGOS:** "the Lord gave the father authority over his children"
**PNEUMA:** "The Lord gave fathers authority over their children"
**Issue:** Greek edoxasen = "glorified/honored." LOGOS/PNEUMA interpret this as authority-giving. EMET is more literal. Consensus: "gave the father authority over his children" — the context is parental rights, so authority is correct.

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.2: "confirmed the right of the mother" vs. "established the right"

**EMET:** "confirmed the right of the mother"
**LOGOS:** "established the right of the mother"
**PNEUMA:** "established the rights of mothers"
**Issue:** Greek esterēosen = "made firm/established." "Confirmed" implies pre-existing right; "established" implies originating it. Consensus: "established the right of the mother."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.6: "give rest to his mother" vs. "brings comfort to his mother"

**EMET:** "whoever obeys the Lord will give rest to his mother"
**LOGOS:** "whoever obeys the Lord brings comfort to his mother"
**PNEUMA:** "your mother will find rest"
**Issue:** Greek anapausei = "will give rest/cause to rest." EMET is most literal; LOGOS substitutes "comfort." Consensus: "brings comfort to his mother" — slightly interpretive but natural.

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.7: "he serves his parents as his masters"

**EMET:** "he serves his parents as his masters"
**LOGOS:** "serves his parents as his masters"
**PNEUMA:** "treating your parents with the same respect you would show a master"
**Issue:** Greek despotais douleusei = "will serve as to masters." PNEUMA paraphrases. All capture the meaning. Consensus: "he serves his parents as his masters."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.9: "strengthens the houses" vs. "builds up the homes"

**EMET:** "a father's blessing strengthens the houses of the children"
**LOGOS:** "a father's blessing builds up the children's homes"
**PNEUMA:** "A father's blessing builds a solid house"
**Issue:** Greek oikous teknōn stereosei = "will make firm/strengthen the houses." EMET "strengthens" is literal; LOGOS "builds up" is interpretive. Consensus: "builds up the children's homes."

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.10: "dishonoring your father" vs. "your father's dishonor"

**EMET:** "your father's dishonor is no glory to you"
**LOGOS:** "your father's dishonor brings no honor to you"
**PNEUMA:** "That brings shame, not glory"
**Issue:** PNEUMA loses the specific reference to the father. All capture the meaning. Consensus: LOGOS reading.

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.13: "if his mind fails" vs. "if his understanding fails"

**EMET:** "if his mind fails, be patient with him"
**LOGOS:** "if his understanding fails, show patience"
**PNEUMA:** "if his mind begins to fail, be gentle"
**Issue:** Greek en pantōs phrenōn autou = "in all of his mind/faculties." LOGOS "understanding" is more precise. PNEUMA adds "begins to" and "gentle." Consensus: "if his mind fails, show patience with him."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.14: "stand as an atonement" vs. "stand as an offering"

**EMET:** "it will stand as an atonement for your sins"
**LOGOS:** "it will stand as an offering against your sins"
**PNEUMA:** "it counts as an offering that covers your sins"
**Issue:** Greek anti hamartiōn antistathmisthēsetai = "will be weighed/counted against sins." The word is not "atonement" (Greek hilasmos) but a balancing/offsetting. "Offering" (LOGOS) is slightly more interpretive but captures the sacrificial parallel. Consensus: "it will stand as an offering against your sins."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.15: "in your affliction" vs. "in the day of your trouble"

**EMET:** "In the day of your affliction it will be remembered"
**LOGOS:** "In the day of your trouble it will be remembered"
**PNEUMA:** "When you are in trouble, it will come to your rescue"
**Issue:** Greek en hēmera thlipseōs sou = "in the day of your affliction." EMET and LOGOS are nearly identical. PNEUMA replaces "remembered" with "rescue." Consensus: "In the day of your trouble it will be remembered in your favor."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.15: "like frost in fair weather" vs. "like morning frost burned off by the sun"

**EMET:** "like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away"
**LOGOS:** "like frost in sunshine, your sins will melt"
**PNEUMA:** "Like morning frost burned off by the sun, your sins will disappear"
**Issue:** Greek hōsei krystalos en eudia = "like ice/frost in clear weather." PNEUMA adds "burned off" and "morning." Consensus: "like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away."

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.17: "perform your tasks with humility" vs. "go about your work with humility"

**EMET:** "perform your tasks with humility"
**LOGOS:** "go about your work with humility"
**PNEUMA:** "go about your work quietly and humbly"
**Issue:** Greek en prautēti ta erga sou diexage = "conduct your works in meekness." PNEUMA adds "quietly." Consensus: "go about your work with humility."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.17: "loved more than a giver of gifts" vs. "more beloved than any lavish giver"

**EMET:** "loved more than a giver of gifts"
**LOGOS:** "loved more than a generous giver"
**PNEUMA:** "more beloved than any lavish giver"
**Issue:** Greek para doton charismaton = "more than a giver of gifts of grace." All reasonable. Consensus: "loved more than a giver of gifts."

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.19: "lofty and renowned" vs. "great and renowned"

**EMET:** "many are lofty and renowned"
**LOGOS:** "many are great and renowned"
**PNEUMA:** "many are exalted and celebrated"
**Issue:** Greek opsēloi kai endoxoi = "high and glorious." EMET "lofty" is literal. LOGOS "great" is interpretive. Consensus: "many are great and renowned."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.19: "mysteries" vs. "secrets"

**EMET:** "to the humble he reveals his mysteries"
**LOGOS:** "to the humble he reveals his secrets"
**PNEUMA:** "God shares his secrets with those who are humble"
**Issue:** Greek apokryptei ta mystēria autou = "reveals his mysteries." "Mysteries" (EMET) is more theologically resonant; "secrets" (LOGOS) is plainer. Consensus: "to the humble he reveals his secrets" — less ecclesiastical.

---

## Disagreement 015 — v.21: "seek not what is too difficult" vs. "do not seek what is too hard"

**EMET:** "Seek not what is too difficult for you"
**LOGOS:** "Do not seek what is too hard for you"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't chase after what is too hard for you"
**Issue:** Greek sklērotera sou mē zētei = "do not seek things harder than you." Minor. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 016 — v.24: "wrong opinion has warped their thinking" vs. "false imagination has caused their thinking to slip"

**EMET:** "wrong opinion has warped their thinking"
**LOGOS:** "false imagination has caused their thinking to slip"
**PNEUMA:** "faulty thinking has caused their judgment to collapse"
**Issue:** Greek hypolepsis planē = "false/erring opinion/imagination." LOGOS "imagination" is interesting — hypolepsis can mean a mental conception. Consensus: "false imagination has warped their thinking."

---

## Disagreement 017 — v.26: "one who loves danger will perish in it" vs. "the one who loves danger will perish by it"

**EMET:** "one who loves danger will perish in it"
**LOGOS:** "one who loves danger will perish by it"
**PNEUMA:** "a person who courts danger will be destroyed by it"
**Issue:** Greek ho agapōn kindynon = "one who loves danger." "Perish in it" vs. "perish by it" — minor. Consensus: "will perish by it."

---

## Disagreement 018 — v.28: "for an evil plant has taken root" vs. "a harmful plant"

**EMET:** "an evil plant has taken root in him"
**LOGOS:** "a harmful plant has taken root in them"
**PNEUMA:** "evil has put down deep roots in that person"
**Issue:** Greek phyton ponērou = "evil/harmful plant." PNEUMA loses the botanical metaphor. Consensus: "an evil plant has taken root in him."

---

## Disagreement 019 — v.30: "atones for sin" vs. "puts out sin"

**EMET:** "almsgiving atones for sin"
**LOGOS:** "almsgiving atones for sin"
**PNEUMA:** "giving to the needy puts out sin"
**Issue:** PNEUMA extends the fire metaphor creatively ("puts out sin"). EMET and LOGOS both render Greek exilasketai = "atones/propitiates." "Atones" is the theologically precise term. Consensus: "almsgiving atones for sin."

---
